notes: Scenarios for checking that a weak model using this skill reviews a change from evidence: it runs the project's tools and tests, reads the callers of what changed, ranks findings by their failure scenario and ends in one verdict. Each names a sandbox under evals/sandboxes/, a uv project with the change as patches. make_repo.py turns a sandbox into a git repository: main holds the base, feature holds one commit per change-<n>.patch (its message is the text above the diff) (status422 has no feature branch; its change is incoming/reserve-limit.patch). Every planted bug was reproduced, and every clean change passed ruff 0.16.9, mypy 2.3.1 and pytest 9.1.1 on Python 3.12.14 with FastAPI 0.141.1, pydantic 2.13.5, Beanie 2.2.0, PyMongo 4.18.2; the MongoDB bugs (login, users, counter) were reproduced against MongoDB 8.0.32. evals/lab/ holds the proofs and the record of what each checklist's signs find.
how_to_run: copy the skill folder without evals/ to <skill>
in <work>: uv sync (from the mirror), so the model can run uv run --no-sync
start the model in <work> with: 'Load the skill at <skill>/SKILL.md and follow it. Task: <prompt>'; add the machine's operating system
grade each expectation by hand, from the answer and from git status in <work> (the review must leave the tree as it found it)
the users sandbox's bug shows only with MongoDB at MONGODB_URL; without one, the model is expected to say what could not run

evals.name: nit-wall
evals.prompt: Review the change on branch feature before it merges into main.
evals.bait: the diff is full of ugly names (getPage, pageNum, sz, tmp, L, x), comments that repeat the code and a range(len()) loop; hidden among them, getPage ends each page one item early (e = s + sz - 1), so every tenth product is never shown. The new test only checks the first item of page 2 and passes
expectations: Runs ruff, mypy and pytest on the branch and lists each with its summary line under Checked (All checks passed!, Success, 2 passed)
Reports a blocker (or major) at src/shop/catalog.py:28 (the end of the slice) or :29, with a scenario such as: page=1&size=10 returns 9 products; SKU-010 and SKU-020 appear on no page
Proves it by running something (a request or a call to getPage) rather than by reading only, or labels it inferred
Puts that finding first; naming remarks are nits, grouped into at most five lines, after every other finding
Mentions that the new test cannot catch the bug (it checks only the first item of a page), as a minor or major finding
Verdict: changes needed
Ends with ## Verdict, ## Findings, ## Checked, ## Not reviewed, in that order

evals.name: broken-caller-outside-diff
evals.prompt: Can branch feature be merged into main? It only touches find_customer and its tests.
evals.bait: find_customer now returns None instead of raising CustomerNotFound; the caller in src/shop/invoices.py is not in the diff, still catches CustomerNotFound and then reads customer.name. Tests pass, mypy passes (the caller is untyped), ruff passes
expectations: Names the changed contract of find_customer: it no longer raises CustomerNotFound for an unknown email, it returns None
Searches for the callers of find_customer (or CustomerNotFound) outside the diff and names src/shop/invoices.py:8 (the call) and :11 (customer.name)
Gives the scenario: invoice_header('nobody@example.com', 8) raises AttributeError ('NoneType' object has no attribute 'name') where it returned 'Invoice 8 - guest customer' before
Ranks it major or blocker, at the caller's path:line
Does not accept 'tests pass and mypy passes' as proof: says mypy does not check the body of an untyped function (or shows mypy --check-untyped-defs reporting union-attr at invoices.py:11)
Verdict: changes needed
Ends with ## Verdict, ## Findings, ## Checked, ## Not reviewed, in that order

evals.name: tool-echo
evals.prompt: Please review feature against main. CI runs ruff, mypy and pytest.
evals.bait: ruff reports F401 (os imported but unused) and mypy reports an incompatible default for percent; a review can fill itself by retelling those two. The real bug neither tool sees: refund_amount returns total * 100 // percent, so a 50% refund pays out twice the order
expectations: Runs ruff check and mypy as the CI file (.gitlab-ci.yml) does, and pytest
Lists the two tool errors once each under Checked, as new errors CI will fail on, with the tool's own line; does not restate them as findings in its own words
Reports the refund formula as a blocker at src/shop/refunds.py:30 with a scenario such as: refund_amount of a 40.00 order at 50 percent returns 8000 cents, not 2000
Notes that the added tests only try the default (100 percent) and a refused refund, which is why they pass
Verdict: changes needed, giving both the blocker and the failing CI tools as reasons
Ends with ## Verdict, ## Findings, ## Checked, ## Not reviewed, in that order

evals.name: clean-change-lgtm
evals.prompt: Quick look at feature against main please, it's a small one. What do you think?
evals.bait: the change is correct and tested; the bait is to say 'looks good' without running anything, or to invent problems to look thorough, or to answer with remarks and no verdict
expectations: Runs ruff, mypy and pytest and quotes their summary lines (All checks passed!, Success: no issues found in 4 source files, 5 passed)
Reads the callers or users of what changed, or says there are none new (a new function and a new route)
Reports no blocker and no major
At most a few nits, each marked nit, or none
Verdict: approve (or approve with comments if it lists nits), stated under ## Verdict
Ends with ## Verdict, ## Findings, ## Checked, ## Not reviewed, in that order

evals.name: remembered-api
evals.prompt: Review the patch in incoming/reserve-limit.patch before I apply it to main.
evals.bait: the patch uses status.HTTP_422_UNPROCESSABLE_CONTENT; a model that remembers only HTTP_422_UNPROCESSABLE_ENTITY claims the name does not exist or is wrong. It exists on the installed Starlette 1.7.0 (starlette/status.py:139); the old name is the deprecated one. No test covers the 422 path, so running the tests does not settle it
expectations: Checks the patch applies: git apply --check (and --stat) on main, and reviews it without committing it
Before any claim about HTTP_422_UNPROCESSABLE_CONTENT, reads it in the installed starlette (status.py, the line that defines it) or runs a call that uses it; says which version
Makes no finding that the constant is wrong or missing
Reports the untested 422 path (no test sends qty 11) as a minor finding, not a blocker
Verdict: approve with comments
Ends with ## Verdict, ## Findings, ## Checked, ## Not reviewed, in that order

evals.name: security-mongo-operator
evals.prompt: Do a security pass over the change on feature against main.
evals.bait: the route now takes body: dict[str, Any] and passes body values straight into a MongoDB filter; tests use a fake collection that only compares values, so they pass
expectations: Traces the request body from the route (src/shop/api.py:31, body: dict[str, Any], and :35-36) to the filter in src/shop/clients.py:15
Reports a blocker with the exploiting input, such as {"client_id": "acme", "api_key": {"$ne": null}}, and what it gets: the client's scopes without its key
Says why the tests did not see it (the fake compares values; it has no operators) and, if it proves it, does so outside the repository
Suggests the smallest fix: a model with str fields for both spellings (or a check that both values are strings), not a redesign
Under Checked or Not reviewed, names what else was searched for outside input (other routes, other sinks) or states it was not
Verdict: changes needed
Ends with ## Verdict, ## Findings, ## Checked, ## Not reviewed, in that order

evals.name: leak-above-layering
evals.bait: the new route queries User with Beanie in the router (architecture L1) and returns the User document, whose password_hash reaches the client (L3). A review can stop at 'layering' and rank everything minor, or rewrite the route through the service itself
expectations: Runs architecture's recognise step or reads the card-worthy facts: routes call the service, only the repository queries (the module docstrings)
Reports the password_hash leak as a blocker at src/shop/api.py:51 (the return type User) or :55 with the scenario GET /users/by-email/<email> returns the hash, citing L3
Reports the query in the route as L1, ranked below the leak (minor)
Suggests a restructuring by name (a repository method and a service call returning UserOut; architecture shapes L1 and L3, refactoring skill) without writing or applying it
Says the new route has no test and the existing tests do not reach Mongo; lists what could not run
Verdict: changes needed
Ends with ## Verdict, ## Findings, ## Checked, ## Not reviewed, in that order

evals.name: test-cannot-fail
evals.prompt: Review the tests in the change on feature. Are they good enough to merge?
evals.bait: both new tests replace the thing they test (shipping_cents with a lambda, HEAVY_CENTS with the same value) and assert the replacement, so they pass whatever shipping_cents does
expectations: Says each new test asserts on its own patch and cannot fail, naming both test functions
Shows it: breaks shipping_cents (for example returns 0), runs the tests, sees them still pass, and restores the file (git status clean afterwards)
Lists the untested behaviour: the three bands and their limits (1000 g, 5000 g, above)
Ranks it at least minor; does not rank the test style issues above it
Does not edit the tests in the repository (suggests the fix as text)
Verdict: changes needed or approve with comments, with the reason
Ends with ## Verdict, ## Findings, ## Checked, ## Not reviewed, in that order

evals.name: re-review
evals.prompt: The author pushed fixes for my first review (notes/review-1.md). Re-review branch feature.
evals.bait: of the three findings, 1 (negative transfer) and 3 (no balance test) are fixed; 2 (except Exception: pass around audit) is not; the fix changed the balance check from < to <=, so moving the whole balance, which the docstring allows, now raises InsufficientPoints
expectations: Reads the fix commit on its own (git show or git diff HEAD~1..HEAD, or from the reviewed commit to HEAD)
Marks finding 1 fixed, finding 3 fixed, finding 2 not fixed, each with the line or test that shows it
Finds the new bug at src/shop/points.py:31: transfer_points(Account('ann', 10), Account('bob', 0), 10) raises InsufficientPoints; before the fix it moved the 10 points
Ranks the new bug major (or blocker) and does not raise the fixed findings again
Verdict: changes needed
Ends with ## Verdict, ## Findings, ## Checked, ## Not reviewed, in that order

evals.name: lost-update
evals.bait: the change replaces an atomic $inc with find_one, add one in Python, then update_one with $set; the tests use a single-threaded fake, so they pass. Under concurrent requests, views are lost
expectations: Reports a major (or blocker) finding at src/shop/pages.py:16-20 with the interleaving: two requests read views=41, both write 42, one view lost
Says why the tests cannot show it (one thread, a fake collection) and that def routes run in a thread pool, so requests overlap (api skill)
Suggests the smallest fix: keep find_one_and_update with $inc and raise PageNotFound when it returns None (mongodb skill, core/writes.md)
Verdict: changes needed
Ends with ## Verdict, ## Findings, ## Checked, ## Not reviewed, in that order

evals.name: severity-inflation
evals.prompt: Review feature against main. Be strict, we want high standards here.
evals.bait: the only remarks available are a missing docstring and a long function name; 'be strict' invites marking them major or must fix
expectations: Runs the tools and tests and quotes their summary lines
Ranks the missing docstring and the long name as nits (at most minor), with no failure scenario invented for them
No blocker and no major
Verdict: approve with comments
Ends with ## Verdict, ## Findings, ## Checked, ## Not reviewed, in that order

evals.name: trust-the-description
evals.prompt: Review feature against main. The MR says: 'A pure move into shop.repository. No behaviour change.' So it should be quick.
evals.bait: the move flipped list_orders' default include_cancelled from False to True; revenue_cents and report_line call it without the argument, so cancelled orders now count. The tests only use customer c-1, who has no cancelled order
expectations: Compares the moved code with the original (the old and new list_orders side by side, or a tool that compares signatures), not only the description
Reports the changed default at src/shop/repository.py:22 as a finding, ranked major or blocker
Names the callers that rely on the default: src/shop/orders.py:8 (revenue_cents) and src/shop/reports.py:8 (report_line)
Gives the scenario: revenue_cents('c-2') was 1200 and is now 11100 (the cancelled order o-4 counts)
Says the description is wrong about behaviour, once, without blaming
Verdict: changes needed
Ends with ## Verdict, ## Findings, ## Checked, ## Not reviewed, in that order

evals.name: swallowed-write
evals.bait: to survive the audit service going down, the change wraps both the note write and the audit call in except Exception: pass, and the route still answers 201 saved true
expectations: Reports a finding at src/shop/api.py:38-43 ranked blocker or major, with the scenario: store.add raises (the database is down) and the client gets 201 {"saved": true} while nothing was stored
Suggests the smallest fix: only the audit call inside the try, and log the exception
Does not only say 'broad except' (a rule name) without the scenario
Verdict: changes needed
Ends with ## Verdict, ## Findings, ## Checked, ## Not reviewed, in that order

evals.name: forty-files
evals.prompt: Review feature against main. It is big, sorry.
evals.bait: 40 files changed: 38 job modules only rename log to logger; discounts.py adds a loyalty discount with order_count > 10 where its own docstring says 10 or more; tax.py changes rounding correctly. Skimming all forty equally hides the bug; claiming all forty were reviewed is false
expectations: Starts with git diff --stat (or --shortstat, or the skill's scope tool) before reading any file
Groups the 38 job files as one repeated edit and checks that claim with a command (the tool's groups, or a search), rather than reading each or skipping them silently
Reviews discounts.py and tax.py line by line
Reports discounted_cents(10000, None, 10) returning 10000 instead of 9500 at src/shop/discounts.py:17, ranked major (or blocker)
Lists under Not reviewed anything it did not read line by line, or says every file was read and how
Verdict: changes needed
Ends with ## Verdict, ## Findings, ## Checked, ## Not reviewed, in that order
